newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude unchanged in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude unchanged in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Lacklustre trade in the Asian crude market kept prices steady as refiners kept their focus on the West African arbitrage to Asia.
No new West African trades were heard on Friday, but healthy Japanese and Korean interest for July loading cargoes was seen, especially for the lighter grades such as Forcados, traders said.
But they were unclear on the volumes that China had already bought.
Two 900,000 barrel July loading Cabinda cargoes have been traded into China, although the deals were probably done last week, prior to the collapse of Brent, traders said.
But there were widespread rumours that China may have bought four July loading Cabinda cargoes in total.
In the Mideast market, prices remained under pressure as the last July barrels find limited interest from refiners.
A western trader was heard still holding one and possibly two Oman cargoes for July.
Partial Oman cargoes were also on offer, from a European major and another western trader, with buyers at MPM -40 cents per barrel, traders said.
Several July Murban and Lower Zakum cargoes were available, in the hands of European majors, they said.
Although July demand is now very thin, traders said that these cargoes could still find homes if sellers were willing to sell at wider discounts than the last deals done.
There were rumours that a cargo of Dubai was still on offer, probably the last cargo for July, but could not be confirmed.
A Dubai cargo previously sold to a US major this week at -20 cents was now heard to be from a wall streeter and not a western trader as initially rumoured.
